title: Rep. Burgess Owens highlights mining workforce bill and small business regulatory relief - West SLC News
text:
Rep. Burgess Owens, U.S. Congressman representing Utah’s 4th district since 2021, addressed issues ranging from workforce development in the mining sector to anti-discrimination measures and small business regulation in a series of posts on December 3, 2025.
In his first statement, Owens emphasized the importance of workforce readiness for the nation’s energy and mineral sectors: “Our nation can’t be a leader in energy or critical minerals if we don’t have the workforce to power it. My Mining Schools Act builds the workforce we need to secure our supply chains, strengthen national security, and unleash American innovation.” (posted December 3, 2025).
Later that day, he took a stance against taxpayer-funded discrimination, stating: “Taxpayer dollars should NEVER fund discrimination.” (posted December 3, 2025).
Owens also commented on recent legislative efforts aimed at supporting small businesses in Utah: “Utah’s small businesses are the heartbeat of our economy, and burdensome big-government mandates have held them back for far too long. @HouseGOP just passed the Small Business Regulatory Reduction Act and the Destroying Unnecessary, Misaligned, and Prohibitive (DUMP) Red Tape Act” (posted December 3, 2025).
Burgess Owens was born in Columbus, Ohio in 1951 and currently resides in Salt Lake City. He graduated from the University of Miami with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1974.
